note: F-148 / R30 route A. PriceBet is the end2end example hand-written in all nine formats (examples/end2end-example/*/PriceBet.*); this fixture holds all seven tiers to one ANF IR and one script hex for it. Every spend below executes the fixture's compiled locking script on @bsv/sdk Spend with real secp256k1 signatures over the real BIP-143 sighash. alicePubKey = alice, bobPubKey = bob, dave is a key neither party holds. The Rabin vector (price 50003, its signature and padding 0x1b under the ~2^260 oracle key) is the one witnesses/real-crypto/oracle-price.json already uses, produced by packages/runar-go RabinSign over num2bin(50003, 8), so the oracle half is not derived from this compiler's output. The winner rows hand the LOSER a dave signature: a valid signature for both parties would let an inverted price > strikePrice branch pass, so each branch has an accept where only the winner's signature is valid and a reject where only the loser's is.

spends.note: price 50003 > strike 50000: alice wins. Only alice's signature is valid (bobSig is dave's), so the accept depends on the alice arm being the one taken.
winner-inversion near-miss: price > strike but only bob's signature is valid. An inverted branch would accept this.
price 50003 == strike 50003: not strictly greater, so bob wins. Only bob's signature is valid. Also pins the > (not >=) boundary.
winner-inversion near-miss: price == strike (bob wins) but only alice's signature is valid. A >= comparison or an inverted branch would accept this.
forged Rabin signature (sig + 1) with both party signatures valid: the oracle check alone must refuse it.
the oracle's signature over 50003 presented with price 50004: the attestation must bind to the settled price.
cancel without bob: the second checkSig fails.
